final_answer: Imagine a world where everyone who wears a silver ring around their neck sleeps better than those who don’t. At first, you might think the ring causes better sleep. But what if the real reason is that people who wear rings are more likely to be relaxed, have stable routines, or simply enjoy the comfort of the ring as a symbol of calm? The ring isn’t the cause—it’s just a sign of something else. This shows that just because two things happen together (correlation), it doesn’t mean one caused the other (causation).
